SDS (sodium dodecyl sulfate) is used in SDS-PAGE to denature proteins and coat them with a uniform negative charge, masking their intrinsic charge differences and allowing separation based primarily on molecular weight.  

Option (A) is incorrect because SDS gives proteins a large negative (not positive) charge.  
Option (B) is partially correct in intent but imprecise — separation is by molecular weight (related to length of the polypeptide), but SDS does more than just allow separation "solely" on that basis; it also denatures and confers charge uniformity.  
Option (C) is incorrect because SDS denatures proteins; it does not prevent denaturation.  
Option (D) correctly states that SDS breaks intramolecular bonds (denaturing tertiary and quaternary structure) and linearizes proteins so they can be sorted by size.  

Final answer: (D)
